collection: Primary4 Igbo family comprehension, roles and interpersonal vocabulary
note: Eighteen original structured drafts:14 written and4 spoken reading/discussion tasks, three original fictional passages, nine additional author mappings. No fixed gender duties, universal household structure, real family disclosure, actual recording/classroom performance or independent native review claimed.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Explain family using suitable examples without assuming a single household arrangement.
questions.prompt: Kọwaa ihe ezinụlọ pụtara n’otu ahịrịokwu. Nye ọmụmaatụ mmadụ abụọ nwere ike ịbụ ndị otu ezinụlọ. Ị nwere ike iji ezinụlọ i chepụtara.
questions.answer: Ezinụlọ bụ otu ndị mmadụ nwere njikọ dịka nne, nna, ụmụaka na ndị ikwu. Ọmụmaatụ: nne na nwa ya.
questions.explanation: The answer gives a general family relationship and an illustrative pair. It does not require every family to have the same members or live in one house.

markingGuide.description: Explains family as a group connected through family relationships in intelligible Igbo.
Gives two plausible related members, without requiring disclosure of the learner’s own family.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Identify named family members and their stated relationships in a fictional description.
questions.prompt: Site n’ederede a, depụta aha nne Ada, nna Ada na nne nne Ada. Kọwaa otu i si mata onye bụ nne nne ya.
questions.answer: Nne Ada bụ Uju. Nna Ada bụ Obi. Nne nne Ada bụ Akụnne, n’ihi na Akụnne bụ nne Uju, Uju bụkwa nne Ada.
questions.explanation: The maternal-grandmother relationship follows from two explicitly stated mother relationships; no unstated relationship is needed.

markingGuide.description: Identifies Uju as Ada’s mother.
Identifies Obi as Ada’s father.
Identifies Akụnne as Ada’s maternal grandmother.
Explains the stated mother-of-mother link in intelligible Igbo.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Describe the household contributions of parents and children in a stated family context.
questions.prompt: N’akụkọ Ọrụ ọnụ, kọwaa ọrụ nna Uche, nne Uche na Uche na-arụ. Gịnị ka nke a na-egosi banyere otu ha si arụ ọrụ?
questions.answer: Nna Uche na-asa efere. Nne Uche na-ehicha tebụl. Uche na-edobe akwụkwọ ya n’akpa. Ha na-ekekọrịta ọrụ.
questions.explanation: These are the roles of the fictional characters in this passage, not universal gender duties.

markingGuide.description: Describes the father washing dishes.
Describes the mother cleaning the table.
Describes Uche putting books in the bag.
Explains that work is shared in this particular family.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Answer literal and inferential questions using an original family-related passage.
questions.prompt: Họrọ ahịrịokwu n’akụkọ Ọrụ ọnụ nke na-egosi na ọrụ ahụ abụghị nke otu onye. Kọwaa ihe mere ahịrịokwu ahụ ji kwado azịza gị.
questions.answer: Ọ dịghị onye na-arụ ọrụ niile naanị ya. Ahịrịokwu a na-egosi na ndị ezinụlọ na-ekekọrịta ọrụ.
questions.explanation: The final sentence directly supports the interpretation; a relevant combination of earlier character actions can also support it.

markingGuide.description: Selects the final sentence or identifies multiple relevant contributions accurately.
Explains how the evidence shows shared rather than solitary work.

questions.learningObjective: Identify and explain contextual vocabulary in an original family-related passage.
questions.prompt: Chọta okwu na-egosi ihe Nneka na-eme n’ihe ụmụaka ji egwuri egwu. Kọwaa ihe okwu ahụ pụtara n’akụkọ a. Họrọkwa otu okwu ọzọ ị chọrọ ka unu tụlee.
questions.answer: Okwu ahụ bụ na-achịkọta. Ọ pụtara na Nneka na-etinye ihe ndị ahụ ọnụ. Okwu ọzọ a pụrụ ịtụle bụ na-ehicha.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Read an original family-related passage aloud with intelligible phrasing and meaning.
questions.prompt: Gụpụta Ọrụ ọnụ n’olu ka onye nkụzi nụ. Mee ka ọ doo anya onye na-arụ ọrụ nke ọ bụla. Mgbe ị gụchara, gwa ya ihe ha niile mere mgbe ha rụchara ọrụ.

questions.explanation: A read-aloud task requires actual spoken evidence. The brief follow-up checks the meaning of the final shared activity.

markingGuide.description: Reads the passage with sufficient accuracy to preserve meaning; allow self-correction.

States in Igbo that they sat together to read after the work.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Express and support a view about a family-related passage through a short discussion.
questions.prompt: Gị na onye nkụzi kwurịta Ọrụ ọnụ. Ị chere na ikekọrịta ọrụ nyeere ezinụlọ a aka? Kwupụta uche gị, nye ihe akaebe n’akụkọ, ma zaa ajụjụ onye nkụzi ga-ajụ.
questions.answer: Ee, echere m na ọ nyeere ha aka. Onye ọ bụla nwere ihe ọ na-eme. Mgbe ha rụchara ọrụ, ha niile gụrụ akwụkwọ. Ha nwere ike ikwurịta ọrụ ahụ tupu ha amalite.
questions.explanation: A justified alternative view is acceptable. The learner must connect an opinion to the passage and respond to a further question, not merely recite a slogan.

markingGuide.description: States a clear relevant view in Igbo.
Supports the view using an accurate detail from the passage.
Responds meaningfully to the examiner’s follow-up about how the family could organise the tasks.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Answer literal and inferential questions using an original family-related passage.
questions.prompt: N’Akụkọ nne nne, gịnị mere tupu Obinna abịa? Gịnị ka Ada mere mgbe Obinna jụrụ otú akụkọ ahụ si malite?
questions.answer: Tupu Obinna abịa, nne nne Ada amalitela ịkọ akụkọ, Ada dekwara ihe ndị dị mkpa n’akwụkwọ. Mgbe Obinna jụrụ ajụjụ ahụ, Ada gụpụtara ihe o dere.
questions.explanation: The response distinguishes the earlier storytelling/note-making from Ada’s later use of her notes.

markingGuide.description: States that the story had begun before Obinna arrived.
States that Ada had written important details.
States that Ada read out what she had written when Obinna asked.

questions.subject: Igbo Language

questions.prompt: Gịnị mere nne nne Ada ji kwughachi akụkụ mbụ? Were otu ihe dị n’ederede kwado azịza gị.
questions.answer: Ọ kwughachiri akụkụ mbụ ka Ada na Obinna ghọta ya. Obinna bịara mgbe akụkọ ahụ amalitelarị, jụọkwa otú o si malite.

markingGuide.description: Explains that repeating the beginning helped them understand, particularly the late-arriving Obinna.
Supports this using his late arrival or question about the beginning.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Answer literal and inferential questions using an original family-related passage.
questions.prompt: Otu nwa kwuru na Chidi gụrụ akwụkwọ ahụ n’ụtụtụ. Ihe o kwuru ò dabara n’atụmatụ ikpeazụ? Kọwaa azịza gị site n’ederede.
questions.answer: Mba. N’atụmatụ ikpeazụ, Amara ga-agụ akwụkwọ ahụ n’ụtụtụ, Chidi ga-agụkwa ya n’ehihie. Ederede ekwughị na ha agụchaala ya.
questions.explanation: The passage reports an agreed plan, not completed reading. The answer must distinguish the first proposal from the final plan and avoid turning future actions into witnessed events.

markingGuide.description: Rejects the claim as inconsistent with the final plan.
States the final morning/afternoon allocation correctly in Igbo.
Recognises that the text gives a plan rather than proof of completed reading.

questions.passage:
Akwụkwọ ezinụlọ
Chidi na nwanne ya nwanyị Amara nwere otu akwụkwọ gbasara anụmanụ. Ha abụọ chọrọ ịgụ ya. Amara tụrụ aro ka Chidi gụọ ya n’ụtụtụ, ya agụọ ya n’ehihie. Chidi kwuru na ọ ga-anọ n’ụlọ akwụkwọ n’ụtụtụ. Ha gbanwere atụmatụ ahụ. Amara ga-agụ akwụkwọ ahụ n’ụtụtụ. Chidi ga-agụ ya n’ehihie. Ha kwetara idobe ya n’otu ebe mgbe ha gụchara.

questions.prompt: N’ahịrịokwu Ha abụọ chọrọ ịgụ ya, ndị Ha abụọ na-ezo aka bụ ndị ole na ndị bụ ha? Gịnị ka ya na-ezo aka n’ebe a?

Akwụkwọ ezinụlọ
Chidi na nwanne ya nwanyị Amara nwere otu akwụkwọ gbasara anụmanụ. Ha abụọ chọrọ ịgụ ya. Amara tụrụ aro ka Chidi gụọ ya n’ụtụtụ, ya agụọ ya n’ehihie. Chidi kwuru na ọ ga-anọ n’ụlọ akwụkwọ n’ụtụtụ. Ha gbanwere atụmatụ ahụ. Amara ga-agụ akwụkwọ ahụ n’ụtụtụ. Chidi ga-agụ ya n’ehihie. Ha kwetara idobe ya n’otu ebe mgbe ha gụchara.
questions.teacherSupport: Examiner asks “Ọ bụrụ na ha abụọ chọrọ akwụkwọ ahụ n’otu oge, gịnị ka ha nwere ike ime?” Score the reasoned response, not agreement with the sample.
questions.deliveryNote: Require live or recorded individual evidence. Examiner checks the Igbo wording and task suitability, supplies the stated follow-up, and scores the actual response. Written preparation alone does not establish performance. No actual recording, classroom execution, fixed reading speed, universal accent/tone standard or examiner calibration is claimed.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.topic: Mkpụrụokwu ndị metụtara mmekọrịta ndị mmadụ na ibe ha
questions.learningObjective: Explain interpersonal relationships using an appropriate everyday example.
questions.prompt: Kọwaa ihe mmekọrịta ndị mmadụ na ibe ha pụtara. Jiri otu ọmụmaatụ sitere n’ụlọ akwụkwọ gosi otú mmadụ abụọ si enwe ezi mmekọrịta.
questions.answer: Mmekọrịta bụ otu ndị mmadụ si akpakọrịta. Dịka ọmụmaatụ, ụmụakwụkwọ abụọ nwere ike ige ibe ha ntị ma nyere ibe ha aka ịghọta akwụkwọ.
questions.explanation: A relationship concerns how people interact; a suitable school example makes the explanation concrete without assuming that everyone is related by kinship.

markingGuide.description: Explains interpersonal interaction/connection in intelligible Igbo.
Provides a relevant school example involving two people.
Explains a constructive feature such as listening, cooperation or mutual help.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.topic: Mkpụrụokwu ndị metụtara mmekọrịta ndị mmadụ na ibe ha
questions.learningObjective: Supply suitable relationship-related words and use them meaningfully in context.
questions.prompt: I chọrọ ka enyi gị nye gị pensụl. Depụta otu okwu ị ga-eji rịọ ya nke ọma na otu okwu ị ga-eji kelee ya mgbe o nyere gị ya. Jiri okwu abụọ ahụ mee ahịrịokwu.
questions.answer: Biko; daalụ. Biko, nye m pensụl. Daalụ maka pensụl ahụ.
questions.explanation: The words perform different interpersonal functions: courteous request and gratitude. Equivalent appropriate forms are acceptable.

markingGuide.description: Supplies a suitable courteous-request expression, such as biko.
Supplies a suitable gratitude expression, such as daalụ.
Uses the request expression appropriately in an intelligible Igbo sentence.

questions.answer: Ndo. Aga m eburu akwụkwọ ahụ nye gị.
